title: Simplex filtration of a cartesian semisimplicial derived object
statement:
Use the small semisimplicial ringed total module category $\mathscr M$ of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category] and the exact functors $\ell_p\dashv e_p$ of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint]. Assume every transition $f_\alpha^*$ is exact. Let $B\in D(\mathscr M)$ be cartesian, with derived transitions $\theta^B_\alpha:Lf_\alpha^*B_m\xrightarrow{\sim}B_n$ for $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$, put $B_p=e_pB$, and write $X_p=\ell_pB_p$. There is a sequence of derived objects $F_N$, $N\ge0$, with maps $u_N:F_N\to F_{N+1}$ and $j_N:F_N\to B$ such that $j_{N+1}u_N=j_N$, together with the following structure in $D(\mathscr M)$:
$F_0=X_0$, $j_0$ is the counit, and for every $N\ge0$ there is a distinguished triangle
$$F_N\xrightarrow{u_N}F_{N+1}\longrightarrow X_{N+1}[N+1]\longrightarrow F_N[1].$$
Let $\delta_i:[0]\hookrightarrow[1]$ omit $i$, for $i=0,1$. Define $q_i:X_1\to X_0$ by its adjunct
$$B_1\xrightarrow{(\theta^B_{\delta_i})^{-1}}Lf_{\delta_i}^*B_0\longrightarrow e_1\ell_0B_0,$$
where the second arrow includes the $\delta_i$ summand. The first-stage rotated triangle is
$$X_1\xrightarrow{q_0-q_1}F_0\xrightarrow{u_0}F_1\longrightarrow X_1[1].$$
There is a coproduct $S=\bigoplus_{N\ge0}F_N$ with coprojections $\iota_N$ and a distinguished triangle
$$S\xrightarrow{1-s}S\xrightarrow{p}B\xrightarrow{\partial}S[1],\qquad s\iota_N=\iota_{N+1}u_N,\quad p\iota_N=j_N.$$
The shifted coprojections $\iota_N[1]$ exhibit $S[1]$ as the coproduct of the $F_N[1]$. All statements are in the unbounded derived category; no boundedness or negative Hom hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0D9B (lemma-simplicial-resolution-ringed), 0D9E (lemma-derived-cartesian-shriek), and 0D9Q (lemma-modules-postnikov). Agent-supplied injective-order-map adaptation: replace the full simplex chain complex by the finite normalized simplex complex in each component. The statement supplies derived objects and a distinguished telescope triangle, not only cohomology identifications.

proof.text:
Choose an actual unbounded complex $C^\bullet$ representing $B$, using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the systems description of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. For $p\geq0$ define a complex of total modules $A_p$ by
$$(A_p^q)_m=\bigoplus_{\alpha:[p]\hookrightarrow[m]}C_m^q.$$
For $\beta:[m]\hookrightarrow[k]$, its transition sends the $\alpha$ summand by the transition of $C^q$ to the $\beta\alpha$ summand. These are finite sums, empty for $p>m$; coherence follows from that of $C^q$. For $p>0$ define $d_i:A_p\to A_{p-1}$ by sending label $\alpha$ identically to $\alpha\delta_i$, and put $b_p=\sum_{i=0}^p(-1)^id_i$. All these maps commute with transitions and the vertical differential $d_C$. In $b_{p-1}b_p$ each two-vertex deletion occurs twice with opposite signs, so it is zero. The fold $\epsilon:A_0\to C$ satisfies $\epsilon b_1=0$, since the two deletions of an edge contribute $+1$ and $-1$.

source.place: Tag 0D9B (lemma-simplicial-resolution-ringed), construction of the labelled face complex; agent adaptation to injections with coefficients in the actual complex C.

proof.text:
The component formula and counit formula of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint] give a chain map
$$\rho_p:\ell_p C_p^\bullet\longrightarrow A_p$$
whose $\alpha$ component is $f_\alpha^*C_p^\bullet\to C_m^\bullet$, the transition of $C$. It respects all transitions by the composition law. Since $f_\alpha^*$ is exact, this component represents $\theta^B_\alpha$; cartesianness makes it a quasi-isomorphism. Finite direct sums give a quasi-isomorphism in each component, and exact jointly conservative evaluation from [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category] detects that $\rho_p$ is a quasi-isomorphism of total complexes. Thus its derived image is an isomorphism
$$r_p:X_p=\ell_pB_p\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(A_p).$$
For $p=0$, the composite $Q(\epsilon)r_0$ is the counit: on label $\alpha$ it is exactly $\theta^B_\alpha$, as that node requires.

source.place: Tag 0D9E (lemma-derived-cartesian-shriek), proof (2), componentwise projection comparison; agent injection-only coefficient-complex version.

proof.text:
For $N\geq0$ form the finite horizontal total complex
$$T_N^r=\bigoplus_{p=0}^N A_p^{r+p},\qquad D|_{A_p}=b_p+(-1)^p d_C,$$
where $b_0=0$. Its differential squares to zero: $b^2=0$, $d_C^2=0$, and the mixed terms cancel since their signs are $(-1)^p$ and $(-1)^{p-1}$. Define a total complex $T$ componentwise by the same formula with $0\leq p\leq m$ in component $m$, and transitions as in Step 1. The inclusions $T_N\to T_{N+1}\to T$ are chain maps. In component $m$ they stabilize to $T_m$ for $N\geq m$. Consequently $T$ is their colimit as complexes of total modules: compatible maps out of the $T_N$ define the map in component $m$ using any $N\geq m$; compatibility with a transition $[m]\hookrightarrow[k]$ is checked at $N\geq k$. The fold on $p=0$ and zero on $p>0$ defines compatible augmentations $t_N:T_N\to C$ and $t:T\to C$ because $\epsilon b_1=0$.

source.place: Tag 0D9Q (lemma-modules-postnikov), finite brutal truncations of the simplex complex; agent direct coefficient-complex construction.

proof.text:
The map $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Here is the contraction, performed separately on each component $m$. Write a label as a strictly increasing tuple $v=[v_0,\ldots,v_p]$ in $[m]$. Let $e:C_m\to(T)_m$ select vertex $[0]$ in horizontal degree zero. Define $h$ on a labelled copy of $C_m^q$ by the identity to label $[0,v_0,\ldots,v_p]$ if $v_0>0$, and by zero if $v_0=0$. This raises $p$ by one and lowers total cochain degree by one. When $v_0>0$,
$$b h(v)=v+\sum_{i=0}^p(-1)^{i+1}[0,v_0,\ldots,\widehat v_i,\ldots,v_p],$$
and the displayed sum cancels $h b(v)$ for $p>0$. When $v_0=0$ and $p>0$, only deletion of the initial vertex has nonzero image under $h$, and it returns $v$. For $p=0$, $b h([v])=[v]-[0]$. Thus on the unaugmented horizontal complex $bh+hb=1-e\epsilon$. Since $h$ commutes with $d_C$ and changes $p$ by one, the vertical terms in $Dh+hD$ cancel as well. Hence
$$Dh+hD=1-et_m,\qquad t_m e=1.$$
These identities of finite-sum sheaf maps show $t_m$ is a homotopy equivalence for every $m$. Exact jointly conservative evaluations of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category] imply $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The contractions need not respect transitions; only the augmentation must do so, and Step 3 checked that. This computation uses no bound on $C$.

source.place: Tag 0D9B (lemma-simplicial-resolution-ringed), component simplex contraction; explicit minimum-vertex contraction for the normalized injection complex, extended to the unbounded coefficient complex.

proof.text:
The inclusions and coordinate projections give a degreewise split short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow T_N\longrightarrow T_{N+1}\longrightarrow A_{N+1}[N+1]\longrightarrow0.$$
The quotient differential is $(-1)^{N+1}d_C$, precisely the indicated shifted differential; the horizontal boundary lands in $T_N$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-derived-triangle] to obtain the triangle with those first three objects and maps. Put $F_N=Q(T_N)$ for $N\geq1$, and set $F_0=X_0$, identified with $Q(T_0)=Q(A_0)$ by $r_0$ of Step 2. Define $u_0=Q(T_0\to T_1)r_0$, and use the inclusions for the remaining $u_N$. Transport the quotient terms by $r_{N+1}[N+1]$ to get the required triangles with third vertex $X_{N+1}[N+1]$. Set $j_0=Q(t_0)r_0$ and $j_N=Q(t_N)$ for $N\geq1$. Step 3 gives $j_{N+1}u_N=j_N$; Step 2 identifies $j_0$ with the counit.

source.place: Tags 014I (definition-split-ses) and 014Q (definition-distinguished-triangle); the termwise split sequence of consecutive horizontal truncations, as used in Tag 0D9Q.

proof.text: For the first differential, $T_1$ is literally the cone of $b_1:A_1\to A_0$: its differential on $A_0^r\oplus A_1^{r+1}$ is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_C&b_1\\0&-d_C\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore gives a distinguished triangle $Q(A_1)\xrightarrow{Q(b_1)}Q(A_0)\to Q(T_1)\to Q(A_1)[1]$. Under $r_1$ and $r_0$ its first map is $q_0-q_1$. Indeed the adjunct of $Q(d_i)r_1:X_1\to Q(A_0)$ sends $B_1$ identically to the $\delta_i$-labelled copy of $B_1$. In component $1$, $e_1r_0$ on that label is $\theta^B_{\delta_i}$. Thus the adjunct of $r_0^{-1}Q(d_i)r_1$ is $(\theta^B_{\delta_i})^{-1}$ followed by inclusion into the $\delta_i$ summand of $e_1\ell_0B_0$, using the derived adjunction in [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint]. This is exactly the specified $q_i$. Since $b_1=d_0-d_1$, transport gives the requested first-stage triangle with its stated first two maps.

source.place: Tags 0D9B (lemma-simplicial-resolution-ringed), signed first boundary, and 0D9E (lemma-derived-cartesian-shriek), identity-summand comparison; cone definition in derived.tex (definition-cone).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim] to $T_0\to T_1\to\cdots$ in $\mathscr M=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ on the small total site supplied by [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. It applies to arbitrary unbounded complexes of module sheaves on a site. Step 3 supplies its degreewise colimit $T$. The cited statement gives the derived coproduct $S'=\bigoplus_NQ(T_N)$ and a distinguished telescope triangle
$$S'\xrightarrow{1-s'}S'\xrightarrow{p'}Q(T)\longrightarrow S'[1],$$
where $s'\iota'_N=\iota'_{N+1}Q(T_N\to T_{N+1})$ and $p'\iota'_N=Q(T_N\to T)$. Replace its third vertex by $B$ through the isomorphism $Q(t):Q(T)\to B$ of Step 4. Replace the zeroth summand by $F_0=X_0$ through $r_0$, keeping the other summands as in Step 5. Transport along the induced coproduct isomorphism. This gives $S=\bigoplus_NF_N$, $s\iota_N=\iota_{N+1}u_N$, and $p\iota_N=j_N$, with the required distinguished triangle. No tensor-product preservation or boundedness assertion is needed here.

source.place: Tag 0949 (lemma-colim-hocolim), together with Tag 0A5L (lemma-direct-sums), as packaged by lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim; componentwise finite construction from Tag 0D9Q.

proof.text:
Finally the shift equivalence of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] preserves this coproduct. Explicitly, for any $Y$, its shift adjunction and the coproduct property from Step 7 give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(S[1],Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(S,Y[-1])\cong\prod_N\operatorname{Hom}(F_N,Y[-1])\cong\prod_N\operatorname{Hom}(F_N[1],Y).$$
These are restriction along the shifted coprojections $\iota_N[1]$, so those maps exhibit exactly the asserted coproduct $S[1]$. All complexes and localizations above are unbounded; the only finiteness used was the absence of injections $[p]\hookrightarrow[m]$ for $p>m$.
